deferred.reason: The retrospective balance form compounds the disbursed principal forward and subtracts the accumulated payments, combining two time-value laws in one expression; per the atomicity rule it is a scenario composition, not a new model. The prospective form is the recorded UPV twin direction. Continuation priority: composition support, not new scalar records.
deferred.title: Loan outstanding balance (retrospective method)

gaps: All three records are requires-extension: interest_payment, principal_payment, payment_index and per_period_rate_definition meanings are new; periodic_payment, periodic_rate, period_count and nominal_rate reuse b01/b02 proposals. No runtime projection attempted.
The payment-split records share the UMD amortization example inputs (A=350.30, i=0.15, n=4) across different payment indices, which is intended: t varies the case.
Duplicate search limited to the supplied snapshot plus b01/b02 of this session.
queries: Of a $350.30 loan payment at 15 percent in a 4-period schedule, how much is interest in the first payment?
What part of the final payment reduces principal when the balance is one period from maturity?
What is the monthly rate for a 5 percent nominal rate compounded quarterly?
handoff.review_notes: Arithmetic validated with the kit validator; source fidelity reviewed against the fetched UMD payment-split text and the Annuity article rate passages. Not performed: visual PDF checks (none used), independent measurement beyond published examples and alternate-route derivations. The two payment-split records decompose one payment into complementary parts (they sum to A) without combining independent laws into a scenario formula.
handoff.summary: Batch b03 finishes the loan-arithmetic queue: the interest and principal portions of a scheduled level payment (complementary, summing to the payment) and the per-period rate definition linking nominal APR to the rate per compounding period.

assumptions: Source assumption: fixed-rate loan with equal end-of-period payments; the balance after t-1 payments discounts the remaining n-t+1 payments at fixed per-period rate i.
Application profile: amortization-schedule interest allocation for a fully amortizing loan with no fees or rate changes.
All amounts and rates on one price basis; i is the effective rate per payment period.

gaps: Needs new quantity meanings: interest_payment, payment_index; reuses periodic_payment, periodic_rate, period_count. No current-runtime projection attempted.
Complements the principal-portion record; the two outputs sum to A by construction.

models.inverse_notes: A=I*(1+i)**(n-t+1)/((1+i)**(n-t+1)-1) needs i>0 and n-t+1>=1; checked year 1: 150.00*1.74901/0.74901=350.27 against the schedule payment 350.30 (input rounding). Solving for t needs a logarithm, unsupported and untested. No zero boundary exists for A>0 under i>0: every scheduled payment carries interest; A=0 gives I=0, the admitted no-loan case.
limitations: Zero-rate schedules (i=0) are excluded by guard; interest allocation there is trivially zero and needs no record.
Beginning-of-period (annuity-due) schedules shift every discount exponent and are not covered.
Solving for the payment index t needs a logarithm, unsupported by the scalar grammar.

references.method: UMD payment-split table gives first-year interest $150.00 for A=350.30, i=15%, n=4; recomputation gives 150.015 because the source payment is rounded (exact 350.265), so tolerance covers the propagated input rounding.

references.method: UMD table gives last-payment interest $45.68; recomputation from the rounded payment gives 45.691, so tolerance covers the propagated rounding.

relationship.locator: UMD tutorial: Principal and Interest Payments (I_t = A(P/A,i,n-(t-1))(i) with balance A(P/A,i,n-(t-1)); table for P=1000, n=4, i=15%, A=350.30 giving year-1 interest 150.00 and year-4 interest 45.68).
relationship.original_equation: I_t = A*(P/A,i,n-t+1)*(i), i.e. A times one minus the n-t+1-period discount factor
relationship.translation_notes: Expanded the source (P/A,i,k)(i) factor into scalar form A*((1+i)^k-1)/(1+i)^k with k=n-t+1; no other change. Dimensional check: currency times a dimensionless share stays currency. Guards i>0, n>=1, 1<=t<=n keep the remaining-term count k>=1 and all divisors nonzero. Reference exponents 4 and 1 are within the tooling cap.

assumptions: Source assumption: nominal annual rate r quoted for m equal compounding periods per year with the rate per period applied uniformly (UMD l*m=1 line; article i=j/m with monthly illustration).
The payment period coincides with the compounding period; otherwise convert with the effective-rate record first.

gaps: Reuses the b01 proposed nominal_rate meaning and introduces the per-period rate as the same periodic_rate quantity used across batches; no current-runtime projection attempted.
The nominal-from-periodic direction (r=i*m) is recorded as an inverse, not a separate model.

models.inverse_notes: r=i*m needs m>=1; checked 0.0125*4=0.05 exactly against the article nominal. Admitted boundary m=1 gives i=r (annual compounding). The effective-annual direction is a different record, never a substitution here.
limitations: This is the periodic rate definition, not the effective annual rate; compounding across periods needs the effective-rate record.
Applies when the payment period coincides with the compounding period; mismatched frequencies need prior conversion.
Quoted add-on or flat-rate conventions that do not divide evenly are outside this definition.
